polish.key_or_line: §0 line 16 / §3 'Is $850 worth it?' / §5.3 item 3 ('free intro call ... not in the facts given')
polish.problem: The landing brief's Objective says families 'book a free consultation'. The research treats the free consultation as unconfirmed, and that error carried into the strategy's CTA design.
polish.fix: State in §0 that the free consultation is a brief fact. In §5.3 item 3, replace the sentence with: 'The brief confirms a free consultation. Make it the primary CTA; a free trial *lesson* is still unconfirmed.'

polish.key_or_line: §1 market table row 'Israeli expats abroad ("yordim" families)'
polish.problem: 'Yordim' is a pejorative term. The table also lacks Luxembourg and Monaco, although the brief lists both as French-speaking markets.
polish.fix: Rename the row to 'Israeli expats abroad'. Add a row: 'Luxembourg / Monaco | FR | Small, francophone, euro | FR language, €750 price.'

polish.key_or_line: §2 P3: 'after-school in Sydney is mid-morning in Jerusalem'
polish.problem: Factually off. 16:00 in Sydney is 07:00–09:00 in Jerusalem, depending on DST.
polish.fix: Replace with: 'after-school in Sydney (16:00) is early morning in Jerusalem (about 07:00–09:00, depending on DST), so rabbis must offer early slots.'

fixes.key_or_line: §4 Conversion model: 'Primary: "Get started" / « Commencer »' + §1.4 '🔶 Pending … free intro call' + Measurement events list
fixes.problem: This contradicts the brief, where the primary KPI is consultation_booked and the free consultation is a stated fact. The content files already use 'Book a free consultation', so strategy and copy disagree on the main CTA, and the KPI event is not tracked.
fixes.fix: Set Primary = 'Book a free consultation' / « Réserver un appel découverte gratuit » (short form « Appel gratuit »). Keep 'Ask our assistant' as the secondary CTA. Move 'free consultation' from 🔶 to ✅ in §1.4. Add `consultation_booked` as the first event in Measurement and name it the primary KPI.

fixes.key_or_line: §6.3 Titles: 'Bar Mitzvah Lessons Online with a Rabbi in Jerusalem | Zoom Mitzvah' (67 chars) / « Préparation Bar Mitsva en ligne avec un rav à Jérusalem | Zoom Mitzvah » (70 chars)
fixes.problem: Both exceed the 60-character title limit. The FR title also uses 'rav' where research §6.2 says SEO copy should use 'rabbin'.
fixes.fix: EN: 'Online Bar Mitzvah Lessons from Jerusalem | Zoom Mitzvah' (56). FR: « Cours de Bar Mitsva en ligne depuis Jérusalem | Zoom Mitzvah » (60).

fixes.key_or_line: §2 Messaging hierarchy FR column: « rabbanim israéliens francophones », « Bénédictions de la montée », « La dracha »; §1.1 FR « que leur enfant (ou eux-mêmes) soit vraiment prêt »
fixes.problem: 'Rabbanim' is an insider Hebrew plural, not public FR copy (the glossary says 'rabbin'). « Bénédictions de la montée » is cut off. The §1.1 agreement is broken. 'dracha' differs from the glossary's 'drasha', and one of the two must win.
fixes.fix: Use « des rabbins israéliens francophones », « Les bénédictions de la montée à la Torah », and §1.1: « …qui veulent que leur enfant soit vraiment prêt pour sa Bar ou Bat Mitsva (ou s’y préparer eux-mêmes)… ». Keep « dracha » and tell Script to update the glossary (see H).

fixes.key_or_line: §2 level 7 'One complete course: $850 / €750' and §7.1 angle 7 '…One course, $850.'; §6.1 'Online tutoring' cluster vs glossary ban on 'tutor'
fixes.problem: (a) The USD display contradicts geo doc §7: outside the US it should read 'US$850', and in FR « 850 $ US ». (b) The #1 money keyword is 'bar mitzvah tutor online', but the glossary bans 'tutor', so the landing meta never targets it.
fixes.fix: (a) Write '$850 (US) / US$850 elsewhere' and point to geo §7. (b) Add a rule to §6: "'tutor' is allowed in meta descriptions, ad keywords and one comparison guide; never in brand headlines". Ask Script to add the same exception to the glossary.

fixes.key_or_line: §4 section table (16 sections) vs content/landing.*.json (11 sections)
fixes.problem: Strategy sections 3 (empathy), 7 (Jerusalem emotion), 8 (AI assistant spotlight + 'Try it now'), 12 (learning differently) and 13 (Adults + 'Learning for myself' CTA) have no keys in the copy files. The plan never reached implementation.
fixes.fix: Add a 'Section → JSON key' mapping column to the §4 table, mark which sections are MVP (at least 8 AI assistant, 12 learning differently and 13 Adults), and hand the list to Script.

polish.problem: The brief (must-have 5) fixes limestone #F3EBDD, night blue #0F1E3A and gold #C9A24A. The guide silently uses different hex values.
polish.fix: Use the brief's hex values, or add a line 'Deviation from brief: … because …' and get the owner's sign-off. With the brief values, gold on night is 6.91:1 (AA) and gold on limestone is 2.03:1 (decoration only). Update the contrast table either way.

polish.key_or_line: §6 reduced-motion CSS block vs rule 'Only instant or ≤150ms opacity fades remain'
polish.problem: The CSS forces every transition to 0.01ms, which contradicts the stated rule. Developers will implement the CSS.
polish.fix: Remove the conflict: either keep the CSS and change the rule to 'all motion becomes instant', or exempt `.fade` with `transition: opacity 150ms`.

polish.problem: No minimum size, clear-space or favicon/social-avatar guidance.
polish.fix: Add minimum width (e.g. 120px), clear space (= cap height) and a square monogram for favicon/WhatsApp/social avatars.

polish.key_or_line: §7.1 'Not in [Country]? Change region' / « Vous n'êtes pas en [Pays] ? »
polish.problem: The FR preposition is wrong for most countries (au Canada, aux États-Unis, au Maroc). EN needs an article ('the United States', 'the UK').
polish.fix: EN: 'Detected location: [Country] · Change region'. FR: « Pays détecté : [Pays] · Changer de région » (no preposition needed). Also « Prix en dollars américains (US). » → « Prix en dollars américains. »

polish.problem: When geo fails, a Dutch-speaking visitor in Europe/Brussels (or a German speaker in Europe/Luxembourg) gets FR. That breaks the BE+nl and LU+de/lb → EN rule in §4.
polish.fix: Before the FR_TZ line, add `else if (/^(nl|de|lb)/.test(primary)) lang = 'en';`, and add QA row 21: geo fails · nl-BE · Europe/Brussels → EN · €750.

polish.problem: Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon and Saint-Barthélemy use the euro but are OCTs, not EU territory. The price result is correct; only the label is wrong.
polish.fix: Split the list: 'EU outermost regions: GP, MQ, GF, RE, YT, MF; Åland AX' and 'French collectivities using the euro (not EU): PM, BL'.

progress_notes: Planning is strong. Research (8.5), brand guide (8.4) and geo rules (8.5) are approved and grounded in honest sources. The customer-facing copy is fluent, the FR typography is impeccable, and keys and placeholders are identical. The track is not ready to ship. (1) EN and FR landing copy carry an unconfirmed promise about teaching each family's tradition (safety cap). (2) The core promise drifted from 'from Jerusalem' to the contradictory 'in Israel … without leaving home'. (3) Strategy, copy, glossary and geo rules disagree on the primary CTA, the USD display and FR 'drasha/dracha'. (4) WhatsApp templates would be rejected by Meta. (5) Nothing is verified in the Lovable build yet: /en /fr routes, hreflang, geo pricing, articles hub and reduced-motion are untested against brief must-haves 1, 2, 4 and 5. Owner blockers: research §8 Q1–Q7, above all the traditions taught, the Bat Mitzvah scope, the number of lessons and the refund policy.
notes_he: סבב 1: שלושה תוצרים אושרו (מחקר, מדריך מותג, כללי גאו). חמישה חוזרים לעיבוד: אסטרטגיה, דף נחיתה EN, דף נחיתה FR, מיילים/ווטסאפ ומילון מונחים. דפי הנחיתה הוגבלו לציון 5 בגלל הבטחה לא מאומתת שהרב ילמד את המסורת של המשפחה (מרוקאית/תוניסאית).
